content.text: No minimum purchase or take-or-pay obligation is imposed on Sanofi anywhere in the agreement, and Sanofi retains a for-convenience exit. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall payment or volume cap on us. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "take or pay" and "commit to purchase" return nothing relevant. Article VII (Manufacturing and Supply) contemplates a future Supply Agreement with price at [***] but sets no committed volumes (p0360); the Commercialization Plan forecasts and net sales projections are expressly "non-binding" (p0370, p0371, p0373). Our financial obligations are usage/activity-based: reimbursement of actual RevMed R&D Costs incurred per an agreed Budget (capped at a stated percentage of budgeted amounts), one-time milestone payments on achievement (capped at $520,000,000), and royalties on Net Sales. In addition, Sanofi holds a broad termination-for-convenience right in its entirety or on a country/Product basis (p0488), so even the funding commitments are exitable. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only); no redline required. We note only that Sanofi carries Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence obligations (§5.7) and cost-share percentages for 2019-2020, which are effort/cost-sharing terms rather than volume or spend commitments and are addressed under other rules.
